summary: Intermittent sawtooth inference latency after client SDK backoff + connection throttling
description:
Issue summary:
SignalWave reports periodic ‘slow’ inference where end-to-end latency spikes in a sawtooth pattern (rise/fall every ~30s) and some requests time out from their client. Impact: product features degrade intermittently for ~10% of requests over 20-minute windows.

Impact:
- Several customers on SignalWave platform show request timeouts and long-tail latency (p95 & p99 elevation).
- SLA alerts triggered for dedicated tenant.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated pool (tenant: signalwave-dedicated-1) in us-east-1.
- Client: SignalWave’s Node SDK v1.4.3 using connection pooling with custom backoff policy (initial 100ms, multiplier 2x, max 30s) and maxConnections=8.
- Traffic pattern: bursty batched inference from many short-lived worker processes (serverless-like).

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Start 200 short-lived workers that each request generation with stream=true to redwood-13b-v2.
2) Workers use SDK connection pool with maxConnections=8 and per-request retry on 5xx/429 with the backoff above.
3) Observe p95/p99 on the customer side and see many connection resets.

Logs / Evidence:
- Customer provided traces: https://observability.signalwave.com/trace/adc12 (redacted session).
- Support capture: API gateway logs show many 502/504 responses clustered after retry storms.
- Serving runtime dashboard: CPU/GPU utilization steady, queue_depth shows periodic spikes aligned to client retry bursts.
- SDK metrics from customer: connection_utilization ~100% preceding spike; retry_count spikes from baseline ~2 to ~120 in 60s window.

Expected behavior:
- SDK should maintain steady throughput with retries being staggered to avoid synchronized bursts. Connection pool should avoid head-of-line blocking and should not exhaust upstream capacity causing cascading timeouts.

Additional context:
- Customer says behavior started after rolling SDK v1.4.3 two weeks ago. Prior to that they used v1.3.7 without issues.
- Customer uses custom exponential backoff without jitter and short maxConnections to conserve sockets per worker.

investigation_notes: Observed pattern: 'sawtooth' latency correlated with retry_count spikes across many tenants using short-lived worker processes.

API gateway's upstream connection pool (per-IP) became saturated when many workers reused identical backoff without jitter; this caused head-of-line request queuing and intermittent 502/504 responses.
Serving runtime remained healthy (GPU mem/compute steady). Problem localized to connection/timeouts and front-end queueing due to synchronized client retries.
Reproduction in staging: enabling full jitter in client backoff and increasing per-worker maxConnections from 8 -> 32 flattened latency curve and eliminated 502 episodes.
SDK regression: v1.4.3 reduced effective jitter window and changed backoff ceilings; combined with small pools, this allowed many clients to re-attempt in lockstep.

Risk assessment: Many customers running serverless or short-lived process patterns with default small connection pools are at risk. Dedicated tenants with constrained upstream connection limits are most likely to show timeouts.
Next steps proposed: short-term customer mitigation guidance, SDK patch to reintroduce conservative jitter as default, and a Console best-practice doc for connection pooling on serverless workloads.
resolution:
Workaround: Customer applied full-jitter randomized backoff and increased SDK maxConnections to 32 for short-lived worker use; this eliminated sawtooth spikes in their tests.

Fix / Rollout: SDK patch merged (PR 4821) to restore safer default jitter and add a configuration option 'enableAggressiveJitter=false' for advanced users. Release v1.4.4 scheduled and backported patch to 1.3.x branch.

Follow-ups:
- Docs: Publish 'Connection pooling & backoff best practices' in Console and SDK README.
- Monitoring: Add dashboard alert for synchronized retry storms (gateway retry_count > 50/min + connection_utilization > 90%).
- Support playbook: Add KB article and triage checklist for retry storms.

Status: Partial fix shipped to SDK repo; customer workaround validated. Scheduled full release and documentation by 2026-03-16.
